{{Short description|Integral transform generalizing both Laplace and Sumudu transforms}}
{{COI|date=June 2025}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Shehu transform''' is an [[integral transform]] which generalizes both the [[Laplace transform]]<ref>https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00377050</ref> and the [[Sumudu transform]]<ref>https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0020739930240105</ref>. It was introduced by Shehu Maitama and Weidong Zhao<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Maitama |first1=Shehu |last2=Zhao |first2=Weidong |date=2019-02-24 |title=New Integral Transform: Shehu Transform a Generalization of Sumudu and Laplace Transform for Solving Differential Equations |url=https://www.etamaths.com/index.php/ijaa/article/view/1771 |journal=International Journal of Analysis and Applications |language=en |volume=17 |issue=2 |pages=167–190 |issn=2291-8639}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Maitama |first1=Shehu |last2=Zhao |first2=Weidong |date=2021 |title=New Laplace-type integral transform for solving steady heat-transfer problem |url=https://doiserbia.nb.rs/Article.aspx?id=0354-98361900160M |journal=Thermal Science |volume=25 |issue=1 Part A |pages=1–12|doi=10.2298/TSCI180110160M |arxiv=1905.06157 }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> in 2019 and applied to both [[ordinary differential equation]] and [[partial differential equation]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Akinyemi |first1=Lanre |last2=Iyiola |first2=Olaniyi S. |date=2020 |title=Exact and approximate solutions of time-fractional models arising from physics via Shehu transform |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/mma.6484 |journal=Mathematical Methods in the Applied Sciences |language=en |volume=43 |issue=12 |pages=7442–7464 |doi=10.1002/mma.6484 |bibcode=2020MMAS...43.7442A |issn=1099-1476|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Maitama |first1=Shehu |last2=Zhao |first2=Weidong |date=2021-03-16 |title=Homotopy analysis Shehu transform method for solving fuzzy differential equations of fractional and integer order derivatives |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40314-021-01476-9 |journal=Computational and Applied Mathematics |language=en |volume=40 |issue=3 |page=86 |doi=10.1007/s40314-021-01476-9 |issn=1807-0302|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Yadav |first1=L. K. |last2=Agarwal |first2=G. |last3=Gour |first3=M. M. |last4=Akgül |first4=A. |last5=Misro |first5=Md Yushalify |last6=Purohit |first6=S. D. |date=2024-04-01 |title=A hybrid approach for non-linear fractional Newell-Whitehead-Segel model |journal=Ain Shams Engineering Journal |volume=15 |issue=4 |article-number=102645 |doi=10.1016/j.asej.2024.102645 |issn=2090-4479|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sartanpara |first1=Parthkumar P. |last2=Meher |first2=Ramakanta |date=2023-01-01 |title=A robust computational approach for Zakharov-Kuznetsov equations of ion-acoustic waves in a magnetized plasma via the Shehu transform |journal=Journal of Ocean Engineering and Science |volume=8 |issue=1 |pages=79–90 |doi=10.1016/j.joes.2021.11.006 |bibcode=2023JOES....8...79S |issn=2468-0133|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abujarad |first1=Eman S. |last2=Jarad |first2=Fahd |last3=Abujarad |first3=Mohammed H. |last4=Baleanu |first4=Dumitru |date=August 2022 |title=APPLICATION OF q-SHEHU TRANSFORM ON q-FRACTIONAL KINETIC EQUATION INVOLVING THE GENERALIZED HYPER-BESSEL FUNCTION |journal=Fractals |volume=30 |issue=5 |pages=2240179–2240240 |doi=10.1142/S0218348X2240179X |bibcode=2022Fract..3040179A |issn=0218-348X|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mlaiki |first1=Nabil |last2=Jamal |first2=Noor |last3=Sarwar |first3=Muhammad |last4=Hleili |first4=Manel |last5=Ansari |first5=Khursheed J. |date=2025-04-29 |title=Duality of Shehu transform with other well known transforms and application to fractional order differential equations |journal=PLOS ONE |language=en |volume=20 |issue=4 |article-number=e0318157 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0318157 |doi-access=free |issn=1932-6203 |pmc=12040285 |pmid=40299951|bibcode=2025PLoSO..2018157M }}</ref>

== Formal definition ==
The Shehu transform of a function <math>f(t)</math> is defined over the set of functions

<math>A = \{f(t) : \exists M, p_1 ,p_2> 0 , |f(t)|< M \exp(|t|/p_i),\,\,\,\text{if}\,\,\,t\in(-1)^i\times[0,\,\infty) \}</math>

as

<math>\mathbb S[f(t)]=F(s,u)=  \int_0^\infty\exp\left(-\frac{st}{u}\right)f(t) \, dt=\lim_{\alpha\rightarrow\infty}\int_0^\alpha\exp\left(-\frac{st}{u}\right)f(t) \, dt,\,s>0,\,u>0,\,\,\,\,(1)</math>

where <math>s</math> and <math>u</math> are the Shehu transform variables.<ref name=":0" /> The Shehu transform converges to [[Laplace transform]] when the variable <math>u = 1</math>.

== Inverse Shehu transform ==
The inverse Shehu transform of the function <math>f(t)</math>  is defined as

<math>f(t)=\mathbb S^{-1}[F(s,u)]=\lim_{\beta\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{2 \pi i}\int_{\alpha-i\beta}^{\alpha+i\beta}\frac{1}{u}\exp\left(\frac{st}{u}\right)F(s,u)ds,\,\,\,\,(2)</math>

where <math>s</math> is a [[complex number]] and <math>\alpha</math> is a [[real number]].<ref name=":0" />

== Properties and theorems ==
{| class="wikitable"
|+ Properties of the Shehu transform<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
! Property !! Explanation
|-
| '''[[Linearity]]''' ||  For any functions <math>\alpha f(t)</math>, <math>\beta w(t)\in A,</math> where <math>\alpha</math>, <math>\beta</math> are arbitrary constants. Then, the Shehu transform satisfies 

<math>{\mathbb S}\left[\alpha f(t)+\beta w(t)\right]=
	\alpha{\mathbb S}\left[f(t)\right]+\beta{\mathbb
	S}\left[w(t)\right].
</math>
|-
| '''Change of scale''' || Let the function <math>f(\beta t)</math> be in set <math>A</math>, where <math>\beta</math> is an arbitrary constant. Then <math>{\mathbb S}\left[f(\beta
	t)\right]=\frac{1}{\beta}F\left(\frac{s}{\beta},u\right).</math>
|-
| '''Exponential shifting''' || Let the function <math>\exp\left(\alpha t\right)f(t)</math> be in set <math>A</math>  and <math>\alpha</math> is an arbitrary constant. Then <math>{\mathbb S}\left[\exp\left(\alpha t\right)f(t)\right]=F(s-\alpha u, u).
	</math>
|-
| '''Multiple shift''' || Let <math>{\mathbb S}\left[f(t)\right]=F(s,u)</math> and <math>f(t)\in
	A</math>. Then <math>{\mathbb S}\left[t^nf(t)\right]=(-u)^n\frac{d^n}{ds^n}F(s, u).
	</math>
|}

=== Theorems ===
====Shehu transform of integral====

<math>
{\mathbb S}\left[\int_{0}^{t}f(\zeta)d\zeta\right]=\frac{u}{s}F(s,u),
	</math>

where <math>{\mathbb S}\left[f(\zeta)\right]=F(s,u)</math> and <math>f(\zeta)\in
	A.</math><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

====''n''th derivatives of Shehu transform====

If the function <math>f^{(n)}(t)</math> is the nth derivative of the function <math>f(t)\in A</math> with respect to <math>t</math>, then <math>{\mathbb S}
	\left[f^{(n)}(t)\right]
	=\left(\frac{s}{u}\right)^{n}F(s,u)-
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\left(\frac{s}{u}\right)^{n-(k+1)}f^{(k)}(0).
	</math><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

==== [[Convolution]] theorem of Shehu transform ====
Let the functions <math>f(t)</math> and <math>g(t)</math> be in set <math>A</math>. If <math>F(s,u)</math> and <math>G(s,u)</math> are the Shehu transforms of the functions <math>f(t)</math> and <math>g(t)</math> respectively. Then

<math>{\mathbb S}\left[(f*g)(t)\right]=F(s,u)G(s,u).</math>

Where <math>f*g</math> is the [[convolution]] of two functions <math>f(t)</math> and <math>g(t)</math> which is defined as

<math>\int _{0 }^{t}f(\tau)g(t-\tau)d\tau=\int _{0 }^{t
    	}f(t-\tau)g(\tau)d\tau.</math><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

====Shehu transform of Caputo fractional order derivative====
If <math>f\in AC^n(a,b)</math> for <math>b>a</math> and of exponential order. Then

<math>\mathbb S\left[^{C}D_t^{\alpha}f(t)\right]=\left(\frac{s}{u}\right)^\alpha 
{\mathbb S}\left[f(t)\right]-\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\left(\frac{s}{u}\right)^{\alpha-k-1}f^{(k)}(0+)</math>,

where <math>\alpha>0,\,m=1+[\alpha].</math><ref>{{Cite journal | last1=Belgacem | first1=Rachid | last2=Baleanu | first2=Dumitru | last3=Bokhari | first3=Ahmed | title=Shehu Transform and Applications to Caputo-Fractional Differential Equations {{!}} International Journal of Analysis and Applications | url=https://etamaths.com/index.php/ijaa/article/view/1958 | access-date=2026-07-18 | website=etamaths.com | date=26 October 2019 | volume=17 | issue=6 | pages=917–927 }}</ref><ref name=MJMS>{{Cite web | title=Malaysian Journal of Mathematical Sciences (MJMS) | url=https://mjms.upm.edu.my/lihatmakalah.php?kod=2021/May/15/2/199-215 | access-date=2026-07-18 | website=mjms.upm.edu.my}}</ref>

====Shehu transform of Riemann-Liouville fractional order derivative====
If <math>\alpha>0,\,\,m=1+[\alpha],</math> and <math>f(t),\,I^{m-\alpha}f(t),\,\frac{d}{dt}I^{m-\alpha}f(t),\cdots,\,^{RL}Df(t)\in A.</math> Then

<math>\mathbb S\left[^{RL}D_t^{\alpha}
	f(t)\right]=\left(\frac{s}{u}\right)^\alpha {\mathbb S}
	\left[f(t)\right]-\sum_{k=0}^{m-1}\left(\frac{s}{u}\right)^{m-k-1}\frac{d^{k-1}}{dt^{k-1}}I^{m-\alpha}f(0+)</math>,
	
where <math>\alpha>0,\,m=1+[\alpha].</math><ref>{{Cite web | title=DOISerbia - New Laplace-type integral transform for solving steady heat-transfer problem - Maitama, Shehu; Zhao, Weidong | url=https://doiserbia.nb.rs/Article.aspx?ID=0354-98361900160M | access-date=2026-07-18 | website=doiserbia.nb.rs}}</ref>

====Shehu transform of Caputo-Fabrizio fractional derivative====
The Shehu transform of Caputo-Fabrizio fractional derivative in Caputo sense is defined as

<math>\mathbb S\left[^{CFC}{_0}D_t^{\alpha}
	f(t)\right]=\frac{\mathcal{B}(\alpha)}{s+\alpha(u-s)}\left(sF(s,u)-uf(0)\right).</math><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Yadav | first1=Surendar Kumar | last2=Purohit | first2=Mridula | last3=Gour | first3=Murli Manohar | last4=Yadav | first4=Lokesh Kumar | last5=Mishra | first5=Manvendra Narayan | title=Hybrid technique for multi-dimensional fractional diffusion problems involving Caputo–Fabrizio derivative | journal=International Journal of Mathematics for Industry | date=2024 | volume=16 | article-number=2450020 | doi=10.1142/S2661335224500205 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Fractional Shehu Transform for Solving - Fractional Differential Equations without Singular Kernel | url=https://future-in-tech.net/17.3/R-Poltem.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251108091213/https://future-in-tech.net/17.3/R-Poltem.pdf | archive-date=2025-11-08}}</ref><ref name=MJMS/>

====Shehu transform of Atangana-Baleanu fractional derivative====
The Shehu transform of Atangana-Baleanu fractional derivative in Caputo sense is defined as

<math>\mathbb S\left[^{ABC}{_0}D_t^{\alpha}
	f(t)\right]=\frac{\mathcal{B}(\alpha)}{1-\alpha+\alpha \left(\frac{u}{s}\right)^\alpha}\left(F(s,u)-\frac{u}{s}f(0)\right).</math><ref name=jmcs>{{Cite journal | title=Journal of Mathematics and Computer Science- Application of Shehu transform to Atangana-Baleanu derivatives | url=https://www.isr-publications.com/jmcs/articles-8239-application-of-shehu-transform-to-atangana-baleanu-derivatives | access-date=2026-07-18 | website=www.isr-publications.com | doi=10.22436/jmcs.020.02.03 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1=Ashraf | first1=Rehana | last2=Rashid | first2=Saima | last3=Jarad | first3=Fahd | last4=Althobaiti | first4=Ali | title=Numerical solutions of fuzzy equal width models via generalized fuzzy fractional derivative operators | journal=Aims Mathematics | date=2022 | volume=7 | issue=2 | pages=2695–2728 | doi=10.3934/math.2022152 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Jadhav | first1=Changdev | last2=Chinchane | first2=Vaijanath L. | last3=Nale | first3=Asha B. | last4=Dale | first4=Tanisha B. | last5=Thabet | first5=Sabri T. M. | last6=Kedim | first6=Imed | title=A study of fractional electrical engineering problems via the Shehu transform | journal=Research in Mathematics | date=2025 | volume=12 | article-number=2583565 | doi=10.1080/27684830.2025.2583565 | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/27684830.2025.2583565 }}</ref>

====Shehu transform of Atangana-Baleanu fractional derivative in Riemann-Liouville sense====
The Shehu transform of Atangana-Baleanu fractional derivative in Riemann-Liouville sense is defined as

<math>\mathbb S\left[^{ABR}{_0}D_t^{\alpha}f(t)\right]=\frac{\mathcal{B}(\alpha)}{1-\alpha+\alpha \left(\frac{u}{s}\right)^\alpha}F(s,u).</math><ref name=jmcs/>

====Shehu transform of regularized Prabhakar fractional derivative====
The Shehu transform of regularized Prabhakar fractional derivative in Caputo sense is defined as

<math>\mathbb S\left[^{C}D_{\mu,\beta,\omega,0}^{\gamma} f(t)\right]=\left(\frac{u}{s}\right)^{-\beta}\left(1-\omega\left(\frac{u}{s}\right)^{\mu}\right)^\gamma F(s,u).</math><ref>{{Cite web| title=Shehu Transform of Hilfer-Prabhakar Fractional Derivatives and Applications on some Cauchy Type Problems | url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/1405797 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410003446/https://dergipark.org.tr/en/download/article-file/1405797 | archive-date=2021-04-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1=Magar | first1=Sachın | last2=Hamoud | first2=Ahmed | last3=Khandagale | first3=Amol | last4=Ghadle | first4=Kirtiwant | title=Generalized Shehu Transform to $\Psi$-Hilfer-Prabhakar Fractional Derivative and its Regularized Version - Advances in the Theory of Nonlinear Analysis and its Application | url=https://dergipark.org.tr/en/pub/atnaa/article/1032207 | access-date=2026-07-18 | journal=Advances in the Theory of Nonlinear Analysis and Its Application | date=30 September 2022 | volume=6 | issue=3 | pages=364–379 | doi=10.31197/atnaa.1032207 }}</ref>
